items.title: Pay
items.text: RMB 15,000 a month before tax, social insurance RMB 2,700 a month

items.title: Rent
items.text: A provincial capital, rent deduction RMB 1,500 a month, reported at work in January

items.title: Parents
items.text: Shared with a brother, RMB 1,500 a month each

items.title: Side job
items.text: One design job in August, RMB 10,000 before tax, withheld per payment

footnote: Example, figures are made up. Social insurance is set for the example, use your own payslip
notes: Now the example. The figures are made up. Our person is a tax resident with one employer all year, working in a provincial capital with no home of their own there, so they rent. Gross pay is RMB 15,000 a month, 180,000 a year, with no year-end bonus. Their own social insurance and housing fund contribution is 2,700 a month, which is set for the example, so check your own payslip. They told their employer about two special additional deductions at the start of the year: rent, 1,500 a month in a provincial capital, and elderly parents. Both parents are over 60 and they share the 3,000 with a brother, 1,500 each. In August they did one design job for another company, RMB 10,000 before tax, paid directly rather than through a platform, with tax withheld on that payment. No author's fees, private pension or donations. Quick guess before we start: refund or top-up?
